It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of an age that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the endurance of the Word and its survival through the fires of history in this hour? [13, 1184, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who seek to “chain” the Gospel with their “unrighteous deception,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the very ink on the page? [13, 20, 1143, 1392, 1420, 1425, 1450, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a culture that “mocks, vilifies, and censures” the Scriptures, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “record of history” by promising that His testimony will never fail [11, 28, 120, 121, 208, 1197, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the preservation of the Bible is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “declares the end from the beginning” (Isaiah 46:10) [15, 68, 1143, 1397, 1488, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Eternal Decree of Endurance**

**Verse**
“The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever” (Isaiah 40:8). [1198, 1306, 1413, 1684, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Reformed theology—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “God intended His Word to abide forever,” and therefore its survival is a “divine guarantee” that transcends the “degenerating power of sin” (Psalm 119:89; 1 Peter 1:25) [29, 1190, 1198, 1204, 1306, 1420, Conversation History]. While “the form of this world is passing away,” the “unfailing Word” remains “settled in heaven” as the only “total truth” and “absolute divine authority” (1 Corinthians 7:31; Psalm 119:89) [12, 113, 1182, 1189, 1198, 1213, 1214, 1323, 1420, 1503, 1684, Conversation History]. Because “the Word of God is not chained” by time or human effort, it serves as the “pilgrim’s staff” and the “soldier’s sword” for every generation of the “church militant” (2 Timothy 2:9) [11, 25, 41, 123, 1211, 1268, 1283, 1342, 1420, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” to explain the permanence of truth, for “if you are going to boast, boast in this, that you know and understand Me” through the Word that “lives and abides forever” (Jeremiah 9:24; 1 Peter 1:23) [51, 123, 637, 842, 1379, 1406, 1503, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price,” and your “sole objective” is to find “repose of the soul” in a Book that “will outlast its enemies” (1 Corinthians 6:20; John 19:30) [12, 24, 101, 142, 1138, 1197, 1262, 1406, 1445, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the Jews were “entrusted with the oracles of God” and commanded to “not add to it nor take away from it,” yet they often “corrupted and perverted” these good things through “rabbinic tradition” (Romans 3:2; Deuteronomy 12:32) [8, 9, 706, 728, 1352, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our posture, showing that while the “religious leaders” often “neglected the weightier matters,” the “church militant” is now the “pillar and ground of the truth” (Matthew 23:23; 1 Timothy 3:15) [8, 67, 1091, 1102, 1104, 1261, 1284, 1346, 1404, 1694, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: Preservation Through Hostile Circumstances**

**Verse**
“Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away” (Matthew 24:35). [1198, 1204, 1515, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Reformed theology teaches that God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to fulfill His “one continuous plan of redemption,” ensuring that even when kings like Jehoiakim “burn the house of the LORD” or the “scroll of a book,” the truth remains “secure” (Jeremiah 36:23; 2 Chronicles 36:19) [5, 64, 942, 1132, 1143, 1169, 1197, 1304, 1315, 1429, 1515, 1532, 1567, 1616, 1720, Conversation History]. Despite the “noise and tumult” of “savage wolves” and “media empires,” the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” are “protected from human tampering” by the King who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones” (Acts 20:29; Psalm 103:19) [11, 15, 20, 68, 716, 926, 1143, 1185, 1307, 1425, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. This “more sure word of prophecy” is the “traveler’s map” that “cannot be broken” by the “cunning craftiness of deceitful plotting” (2 Peter 1:19; John 10:35; Ephesians 4:14) [13, 296, 345, 595, 785, 855, 1190, 1211, 1313, 1334, 1379, 1406, 1420, 1452, 1453, 1462, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the Word of our God stands forever” even when “earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh” (Isaiah 40:8; Daniel 5:26) [11, 16, 21, 29, 39, 94, 121, 201, 1306, 1408, 1460, 1515, 1684, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to “hold fast what is good,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” to preserve the “spotless purity of truth” (1 Thessalonians 5:21; Job 42:2) [5, 11, 21, 30, 90, 116, 1132, 1342, 1391, 1406, 1408, 1515, 1572, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Mosaic Economy vs. Heavenly Citizenship**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” and the physical survival of the “sanctuary” were “temporal signs” of God’s presence, yet the Lord “removed kings” who “rejected the word of the LORD” (1 Samuel 15:23) [7, 15, 17, 342, 409, 1078, 1183, 1313, 1353, 1519, 1533, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this, revealing that our “victory” is not in “carnal weaponry” but in “the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for our “citizenship is in heaven” (Revelation 12:11; Philippians 3:20) [13, 21, 26, 32, 38, 92, 142, 440, 1023, 1113, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1402, 1426, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Miracle of Faithful Transmission**

**Verse**
“Forever, O LORD, Your word is settled in heaven” (Psalm 119:89). [1198, 1214, 1570, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—notes that “God’s Word was protected from error in its original record by the ministry of the Holy Spirit” and has been preserved through the “exacting science of textual criticism” (2 Peter 1:21) [1193, 1200, 1204, Conversation History]. Though sin causes “tens of thousands of copies” to contain slight variants, “99.99 percent of the original writings have been reclaimed,” proving that “no lie is of the truth” (1 John 2:21) [1202, 1204, 1385, 1512, 1560, Conversation History]. God “ordered those things in his providence” so that even discoveries like the Dead Sea Scrolls confirm that “not one thing has failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spoke” (Joshua 23:14) [15, 695, 753, 975, 1143, 1201, 1312, 1484, 1532, 1567, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for “the LORD Himself is God... there is none other besides Him” and His “everlasting dominion” over His text is “secure” (Deuteronomy 4:35; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 116, 121, 147, 176, 201, 292, 352, 412, 602, 630, 710, 782, 852, 921, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1181, 1214, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” recognizing that “man lives by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD,” and that Word is “totally sufficient for your needs” (Deuteronomy 8:3; 2 Timothy 3:16) [11, 14, 24, 101, 116, 147, 176, 201, 211, 412, 670, 720, 809, 811, 824, 829, 859, 861, 916, 922, 925, 1062, 1132, 1143, 1189, 1191, 1213, 1214, 1312, 1313, 1331, 1406, 1408, 1413, 1414, 1450, 1461, 1503, 1514, 1515, 1532, 1684, 1709, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Forensic Accuracy**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “testifying in a dispute” required “two or three witnesses” to establish a “legal verdict,” a principle that reflects God’s own “standard of utmost accuracy” in His Word (Deuteronomy 17:6) [330, 367, 584, 673, 1012, 1056, 1072, 1230, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “witness,” showing that while we “first experience something” then “rush to the Scripture,” we must “examine everything carefully” to distinguish the “glittery lookalike from the genuine commodity” (1 Thessalonians 5:21) [11, 35, 76, 90, 116, 294, 371, 396, 415, 417, 419, 424, 1017, 1408, 1461, 1513, 1515, 1534, 1709, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Sealed Canon as Final Fortress**

**Verse**
“ ‘For I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues that are written in this book’ ” (Revelation 22:18). [1206, 1214, 1324, 1331, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition asserts that the “canon of Scripture is actually closed, never to be reopened,” because the “foundational age” of “apostles and prophets” has “passed away” (Ephesians 2:20) [94, 121, 123, 385, 389, 422, 449, 581, 584, 585, 1206, 1207, 1208, 1326, Conversation History]. To seek “additional revelation” or “fresh words” is a “spirit of fraud” that “undermines the authority of Scripture” and “competes with the exclusivity of biblical revelation” [11, 95, 122, 186, 317, 343, 345, 348, 359, 361, 402, 403, 558, 598, 1503, Conversation History]. The “complete body of revelation” provides “repose of the soul” and “total truth” because “everything the Sabbath signified has been completely fulfilled in the finished work of Christ” (Hebrews 4:10) [13, 17, 24, 136, 142, 1445, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by those who “label human intuition as divine prophecy,” for “your life is not your own” and you must instead “be filled with the Word” (1 Corinthians 6:20; 1 Timothy 6:20) [12, 91, 101, 116, 273, 528, 646, 697, 1138, 1218, 1262, 1406, 1411, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must find your “joy, satisfaction, [and] contentment” solely in the “inspired Scriptures” (Proverbs 28:26; 2 Timothy 3:15) [13, 20, 32, 79, 99, 110, 116, 274, 1311, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 296, 300, 313, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

The Talmud, the codification of rabbinic traditions, says, “Honour the physician before you have need of him.… The Holy One says, just as it is my office to cause the rain and the dew to fall, and make the plants to grow to sustain man, so art thou bounden to pray before me, and to praise me in accordance with my works; thou shalt not say, I am in prosperity, wherefore shall I pray? But when misfortune befalls me then will I come and supplicate” (Sanhedrin 44b). That is the right perspective. Prayer was not to be used just for emergency appeals; it was to be an unbroken conversation built around a living, loving fellowship with God.

Again we see that the point Jesus is teaching has nothing to do with the skill of the sower or the quality of the seed. The seed is perfect, and eternally unchanging. Any attempt to improve the harvest by using different seed is a misguided dereliction of the sower’s duty. The point of the activity is not merely to produce dense but fruitless foliage. If that were the goal, he could sow dandelions or tumbleweeds. It’s quite true that these would germinate and grow more easily in the shallow, hard, or already weedy places.

Meanwhile, we live longingly, pleading like those under the altar in Revelation 6:10: “How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?” We are among those described in 1 Thessalonians 1:10, who “wait for [God’s] Son from heaven … even Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come.” It is impossible to live the Christian life faithfully unless it is in the light of the Second Coming. Knowing the end of the story gives us confidence and stability. As Paul says, “Be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord” (1 Cor. 15:58).

Further observing that Jesus’ own telling of the prodigal son parable ends without resolution, the article suggests that this “reveals the open-endedness of the Kingdom of God.” What’s more, the story’s true ending “is the end of my story, your story, and everyone’s story—beyond our wildest dreams.” By such a wholly subjective approach, Jesus’ stories become playthings to be bent and shaped into whatever form suits the hearer’s fancy. Jesus’ whole message becomes versatile, subjective, and infinitely adaptable to the felt needs and personal preferences of each hearer.

two Ancient History, Timeless Truth To fully understand the New Testament’s use of slave language, we need to begin with a historical perspective regarding the practice of slavery in the Greco-Roman era. Slavery was a pervasive social structure in the first-century Roman Empire. In fact, it was so commonplace that its existence as an institution was never seriously questioned by anyone.1 Slaves of all ages, genders, and ethnicities constituted an important socioeconomic class in ancient Rome. Roughly one-fifth of the empire’s population were slaves—totaling as many as twelve million at the outset of the first century AD.2 Not surprisingly, the entire Roman economy was highly dependent on this sizable pool of both skilled and unskilled labor.

Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. But unlike the Roman slave market—where slaves were selected based on their positive qualities, like strength, health, and physical appearance—God chose His slaves with the full knowledge of their weaknesses and failures. We “were not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble; but God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the things which are strong” (1 Cor. 1:26–27). Indeed, He mercifully elected us to salvation in spite of ourselves, saving us—not because of any inherent goodness in us—but according to His own eternal purposes and for the sake of His glory.

Later in Romans 8, Paul further underscored the permanence of our adoption. In verses 29–31, he explained that all those whom God has justified, He will glorify; none will be lost. In verses 32–34, he encouraged believers with the truth that no accusation made against God’s elect will ever stick, because all has been forgiven through Christ. Finally, in verses 35–39, the apostle noted that there is absolutely nothing that can separate God’s children from His eternal love. With our adoption complete, our security in God’s family is forever fixed. The astonishing reality of adoption is that believers are given “a place in God’s family just as eternal and secure as His only-begotten Son.”21

Our life is synonymous with our citizenship. Our priorities, passions, and pursuits have all been changed because our very identity has been transformed (Phil. 1:21). Like the saints of old, we no longer chase after the passing pleasures of this world.34 Instead, our eyes are fixed on heaven, our true home, the place where Christ is.35 Whether we go to Him in death or He comes to us in rapture, we will soon be together with Him forever.36 One day we will stand in His presence, as slaves before the Master. One day we will bow before Him, as subjects before the King. As both slaves and citizens, we will serve Him and reign with Him for all eternity. This is the hour for the true church to respond. At a time when there is a revival of the biblical gospel and a renewed interest in the solas of the Reformation, it is unacceptable to stand by idly. All who are faithful to the Scriptures must rise up and condemn everything that assaults the glory of God. We are duty-bound to apply the truth in a bold defense of the doctrine of the Holy Spirit. If we claim allegiance to the Reformers, we ought to conduct ourselves with the same level of courage and conviction they displayed as we contend earnestly for the faith.
